name: חילוק שבר במספר שלם (באנגלית)

generalfeedback:
Outline: Dividing by a whole number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, so the denominator is multiplied by that number; then simplify.
Step 1 — Multiply the denominator by the whole number
When dividing a fraction \(\frac{a}{b}\) by an integer \(c\) you simply multiply the denominator \(b\) by \(c\), because \(\frac{a}{b}\div c=\frac{a}{b}\cdot\frac{1}{c}=\frac{a}{b\cdot c}\). Therefore in this example:

\[ {{CT:0}}\div {{CT:1}}=\frac{{{CT:2}}}{{{CT:3}}\cdot {{CT:1}}}=\frac{{{CT:2}}}{{{CT:4}}} \]

Step 2 — Simplify
[[if test="{{CT:9}}"]]The numerator \({{CT:2}}\) and the whole number \({{CT:1}}\) have the common factor \({{CT:5}}\) (their greatest common divisor). Cancel it:

\[ \frac{{{CT:2}}}{{{CT:3}}\cdot {{CT:1}}}=\frac{{{CT:6}}}{{{CT:3}}\cdot {{CT:7}}}={{CT:8}} \]

[[else]]The numerator \({{CT:2}}\) and the whole number \({{CT:1}}\) have no common factor (their greatest common divisor is \(1\)), so nothing cancels.[[/if]]The fraction \({{CT:0}}\) is already in lowest terms, so the numerator and the denominator of the result have no common factor (greatest common divisor \(1\)). The answer in its simplest form:

\[ {{CT:8}} \]
